query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled, post‐synthesis aging treatment can precipitate a fine, ductile secondary phase along grain boundaries in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38, thereby improving its integrity (crack resistance) while preserving its strong caloric response.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-cast (or rapidly solidified) (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with a relatively coarse microstructure prone to crack formation under applied fields and pressure.
generation.intervention: A thermal aging process immediately after synthesis that is optimized to induce the in situ formation of a fine, ductile secondary phase decorating the grain boundaries.
generation.conditions: The treatment is performed under controlled temperature (e.g., moderate temperatures below the primary phase transition but high enough to allow diffusion) and time parameters such that the aging avoids coarsening. Subsequent caloric performance tests are conducted under the same applied-field, pressure, temperature, and mechanical loading regimes as the untreated alloy.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a fine dispersion of ductile precipitates along grain boundaries that act to blunt crack propagation and improve toughness without interfering with the primary caloric transition mechanisms.
generation.mechanism: Controlled aging produces finely distributed secondary phases that reinforce the microstructure by strengthening the grain boundaries and acting as crack deflection sites. This modification enhances mechanical integrity while the bulk phase transition responsible for the caloric effect remains largely unperturbed.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significant improvement in mechanical integrity is expected: an increase in compressive strength relative to the base alloy (ideally moving toward values observed with epoxy or low-melting composites) with less than a 10% reduction (or ideally negligible impact) in caloric response performance.
generation.baseline: The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, which exhibits high caloric response but poor structural integrity, including a tendency to crack.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable under operational conditions where the alloy is subject to combined field (e.g., magnetic or hydrostatic pressure) and thermal cycling, and where the mechanical loading is representative of typical service conditions. The thermal aging parameters must be chosen so as not to trigger undesirable phase transformations or coarsening.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the exact aging temperature, time, and secondary phase volume fraction that will optimize the balance between improved mechanical strength and preservation of the caloric effect. Additionally, the sensitivity of the caloric response to subtle microstructural changes introduces some risk that even minor precipitate formation could affect phase transition dynamics.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38: one set undergoes the proposed thermal aging treatment and the other set acts as the untreated control. Ensure that all samples receive identical synthesis and initial processing. Conduct comprehensive microstructural analyses (e.g., TEM/SEM) to confirm the formation and dispersion of the secondary phases. Subject both sets to mechanical (compressive strength) tests and caloric response measurements under the same applied field and pressure conditions.
measurements: Caloric effect parameters (e.g., isothermal entropy change or adiabatic temperature change)
Microstructural characterization to verify secondary phase size and distribution
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged samples do not exhibit an improvement in compressive strength (e.g., less than a 15% increase relative to the control) or if there is a statistically significant reduction (greater than 10%) in the caloric response compared to the untreated alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.
